report.summary: (model supplied no summary; its answer is preserved in handoff)

handoff.purpose: Run the advisory regression gate comparing current tier1 results to a stored baseline.

symbols.name: run_gate
symbols.note: Loads baseline, runs tier1, classifies per-task results into regressions/improved/new/errored/focus_withheld, returns a report dict.

claims.text: ADVISORY regression ratchet. Replays ``tasks`` (default TASKS) against a stored baseline.json and flags any PRIMARY-tier task whose recall DECREASED.
claims.why: Tasks default to all_tasks() (line 861); baseline loaded from baseline_path (line 862-863); per_task iterated (line 874); primary-tier tasks with current recall < baseline recall appended to regressions (lines 894-899).

claims.text: Compares PER TASK, never on a mean -- a mean hides one task collapsing while another improves (see tests/test_eval_oracle.py for the mean-preserving-swap test that proves this).
claims.why: Loop compares each task's recall individually (lines 894-899); no aggregate mean is computed anywhere in this chunk.

claims.text: Workflow before shipping a slice-heuristic change: python -m daedalus.eval --gate. Expect PASS.
claims.why: CLI entry point and flag parsing are outside this chunk; only the function body is visible.

claims.text: A FAIL means either a real regression (fix the slicer) or an intentional, reviewed label change -- in which case update the baseline EXPLICITLY (never automatically): python -m daedalus.eval --update-baseline
claims.why: The update-baseline command is not in this chunk; no automatic baseline write occurs here (only load_baseline is called).

claims.text: GUARDRAIL: this gate is ADVISORY ONLY. It is a local developer command plus a unit test (there is no CI in this repo -- verified: no .github/workflows). It must never be wired to block an autonomous action.
claims.why: The advisory flag is set in the return dict (line 914), but whether it is wired to block anything is external to this chunk; CI absence is unverifiable here.

claims.text: ERRORED tasks (see ``run_tier1``) have no recall to compare and are SPLIT by tier, not folded into ``regressions``: * PRIMARY tier -- FAILS the gate loudly (``errored_primary``, named in the rendered report).
claims.why: Error rows are appended to errored_primary or errored_quarantine based on _is_primary_tier (lines 878-883); passed requires len(errored_primary)==0 (line 913); errored_primary is in the return dict (line 918).

claims.text: QUARANTINE tier -- reported only (``errored_quarantine``), never fails the gate -- flywheel debris (an unconfirmed minted task whose target moved/vanished) must not be able to block a developer's gate run.
claims.why: Non-primary error rows go to errored_quarantine (line 883) and are excluded from the passed calculation (line 913 only checks regressions and errored_primary).

claims.text: FOCUS-WITHHELD tasks (the secret floor fail-closed on the task's own focus file -- lane A1) are likewise SPLIT OUT, not folded into ``regressions``: a task that TRANSITIONS to focus-withheld this run has no ``recall`` to compare (fail-closed is not "recall dropped to 0"), so treating it as a regression would be a false alarm on the fence doing its job.
claims.why: If t.get("focus_withheld") is truthy, the task is appended to focus_withheld and skipped via continue (lines 884-886), so it never reaches the regression comparison.

claims.text: Reported in its own ``focus_withheld`` section, regardless of tier, and never fails the gate.
claims.why: focus_withheld list is populated for any tier (line 885, no tier check), included in return dict (line 921), and not referenced in passed computation (line 913).

claims.text: quarantine is never gated, see module docstring
claims.why: After error and focus_withheld handling, non-primary tasks are skipped via continue (lines 888-889), so they cannot enter regressions.
